issues.description: Guard fires for any non-Tab key and may not actually short-circuit the downstream Enter accept path
issues.detail: The condition `not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` triggers the hide+forward branch for every non-Tab key, not just Return/Enter. Worse, the existing Enter/Return/Tab accept logic further down may still run for some items. Restructure as a single 'is this key an accept key right now?' predicate at the top of keyPressEvent.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keystroke in the completion popup hot path
issues.detail: Reading the config dictionary on each keyPressEvent couples the typing hot path to the conf system unnecessarily. Cache the value when the popup is shown or subscribe to config changes. Bind to a named local first so the guard reads cleanly.

issues.description: Manually re-dispatching the event to textedit.keyPressEvent is fragile control flow
issues.detail: Calling `self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` from inside the popup bypasses Qt's structured propagation, couples the popup to the editor's exact event semantics, and risks double-handling if Qt also propagates the unhandled event. Prefer event.ignore()/accept() and let normal Qt propagation deliver it.

issues.description: Awkward expression style: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` instead of `key != Qt.Key_Tab`
issues.detail: The `not x == y` form is a style smell that signals the author transcribed rather than reasoned about the expression. Trivial to fix and matches surrounding code voice. Bind the conf lookup to a named local in the same pass for readability.

issues.description: No test coverage for the new option's two branches
issues.detail: Completion-widget key handling regresses silently. A single test that toggles the preference off, sends Enter, and asserts no completion is accepted (plus the inverse) would protect this from being undone by the next maintainer.

issues.description: Guard wedged mid-handler instead of grouped with sibling key dispatches
issues.detail: The new block sits after `item = self.currentItem()` rather than with the other key handlers at the top of keyPressEvent. Move the early-exit guard above the item lookup so control flow reads linearly and the disabled path doesn't pay for currentItem(). Also confirm the default-True option preserves legacy behavior for upgrading users.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, scoped patch solving a real user problem but lands as a wart bolted onto an already-busy keyPressEvent. The core defects are structural: the guard triggers for any non-Tab key rather than only Return/Enter, the downstream Enter accept path may not be cleanly short-circuited, and the fix manually re-dispatches the event into textedit instead of using Qt's event.ignore() discipline. Secondary concerns include calling get_conf on every keystroke, the `not x == y` style smell, missing tests, and placement of the guard. Needs-work; restructure the key dispatch around a single 'is this an accept key?' predicate, cache the conf value, and add a test.
